newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's McIntosh warns competitors after bid.
newsitem.headline: Australia's McIntosh warns competitors after bid.

text.p: Australia's McIntosh Securities Ltd. said Tuesday it accepted a A$117 million ($92 million) takeover bid from Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc., making it one of the region's leading financial services groups.
Merrill Lynch offered A$1.40 ($1.11) a share for Australia's only listed broker, representing a premium of about 48 percent on McIntosh's average closing price in the last 30 days.
The combined firm, to be known as Merrill Lynch (Australia) Pty. Ltd., would become a market leader in most broker services at a wholesale and retail level, the companies said.
"The combination will be powerful," Chairman John McIntosh told the company's annual meeting. "Should the merger succeed, I will leave you with a final thought -- competitors beware."

Jerome Kenney, Merrill Lynch executive vice president for corporate strategy and research, said the Wall Street firm was also interested in moving into asset management, but had not yet decided how this would be achieved.
"We are very positive about the outlook for this market and we expect to grow this business. We are convinced that this will become a major market for us," Kenney said.
McIntosh unanimously recommended acceptance of the bid, saying its directors would accept the offer for their stock.
McIntosh's board, management and staff hold a total of 36 percent of the company.
The bid, which Merrill Lynch would fund from existing cash reserves, was subject to 90 percent acceptances and U.S. and local regulatory approvals.
Merrill said it already held 19.15 percent of McIntosh.
